statements.text: a driver MUST NOT pass another vehicle WHEN the driver is on a road where a "do not pass" sign is posted

sources.quote: Do not pass on this road.

flags.note: Read as the road where the sign is posted; the passage does not say where the prohibition begins or ends.

statements.note: The caption is a plain imperative; the legal force comes from the regulatory signs section, and the sign itself is identified from the image in m25.

statements.text: a driver MUST keep to the right-hand lane WHEN the driver is on a [?two-lane section] where a passing lane or climbing lane is provided UNLESS the driver is passing

sources.quote: Keep to the right lane except when passing on two-lane sections where climbing or passing lanes are provided.

see.figure: the passing lane or climbing lane sign

flags.note: It is unclear whether the two lanes are the driver's lane plus the added lane in one direction, or one lane in each direction.

statements.note: The caption is a plain imperative; the legal force comes from the regulatory signs section. "On two-lane sections where climbing or passing lanes are provided" is read as limiting the whole rule rather than only the passing exception, which fits the lane-split arrows in the image (m30).

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a pilot vehicle or pace vehicle WHEN the pilot vehicle or pace vehicle bears a "when flashing" sign with the no-passing symbol AND [?the sign is flashing]

sources.quote: Do not pass the pilot vehicle or pace vehicle bearing this sign.

flags.note: Resolved to the temporary condition sign shown in figure m74.
The sign's legend reads "WHEN FLASHING" without saying what flashes, the sign or lights on the vehicle.
The sign carries the same red no-passing symbol as the regulatory "do not pass" sign, but the temporary condition signs section gives no legal wording, so the force stays advisory.

statements.note: The flashing condition comes only from the sign's legend in the image (m74), not from the caption text.

statements.text: FACT a "long" placard indicates a long commercial vehicle

sources.quote: This placard indicates a long commercial vehicle, which is a double trailer and can be up to 40 metres in length. It is important to be able to recognize an LCV on the highway, based on rear signage, and anticipate both the extended length and limited speed when preparing to pass one on the highway.
Title: Long commercial vehicle (LCV) - Description: Long commercial vehicle (LCV)

flags.note: Resolved to the yellow placard reading "LONG" shown in figure m67.

statements.text: a driver on a multi-lane road MUST keep to the right WHEN the driver's vehicle is [?slow traffic]

sources.quote: Slow traffic on multi-lane roads must keep right.

flags.note: No speed or comparison says when a vehicle counts as slow traffic.
The sign in the image says "slower traffic" where the caption says "slow traffic".
